program_name: Master in Accounting and Finance. This is the official English name used on the unibz programme page, on the 2026/27 brochure cover and on the 2026/27 admission-information document. The programme is legally issued in three languages and the other two official names matter because the binding administrative acts (the signed ranking-list decrees) are published ONLY in Italian and German, never in English: Italian 'Laurea magistrale in Accounting e Finanza' and German 'Master in Accounting und Finanzwirtschaft'. Faculty: Faculty of Economics and Management (Fakultaet fuer Wirtschaftswissenschaften / Facolta di Economia). Degree awarded: Laurea Magistrale (second-cycle degree, 120 ECTS, 2 years). Degree Course Director: Prof. Paolo Perego (who also chairs the admission committee and signs the ranking lists as 'Il Presidente / Der Vorsitzender'). Admission committee members named on the 2026/27 decrees: Prof. Nicola Dalla Via and Prof. Massimiliano Bonacchi. Student Representative in the Course Council: Giada Mantovani. Do not confuse this programme with the unibz PhD in Economics and Finance (a separate doctoral programme at the same faculty) or with the Master in Data Analytics for Economics and Management / Master in Entrepreneurship and Innovation, which are the English-taught masters of the same faculty.
level: Master (second cycle / laurea magistrale / Masterstudium). 120 ECTS credit points over 2 years (4 semesters). Italian second-cycle degree in class LM-77. Not a single-cycle programme, not a professional/first-level 'Master universitario' (the faculty runs those separately, e.g. the 1st Level Master in Digital and Socially Sustainable Human Resources Management). The programme qualifies for admission to post-graduate training including PhD programmes: 'This study programme also qualifies to gain admission to post-graduate training, such as a PhD programme.' Simultaneous enrolment in a maximum of 2 programmes is allowed under national law, provided the two programmes are not in the same degree class and differ by at least 2/3 of the course contents.
teaching_language: TRILINGUAL (Italian / German / English) - and this is not a formality: the trilingual character is enforced both at the admission gate and inside the curriculum. The admission document states: 'The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English.' The brochure 'At a Glance' box states: 'Courses will be taught in: Italian, German and English (trilingual)'. ACTUAL LANGUAGE SPLIT IN THE PUBLISHED 2026/27 COURSE OFFERING (each course on the unibz course-offering page carries an explicit EN / IT / DE tag; this is the hard evidence, not the marketing text): (a) FIRST YEAR, compulsory for ALL THREE study tracks - Economics for Accounting and Finance 12 CP EN (M-1 Macroeconomics EN, M-2 Industrial Economics EN); Applied Statistics for Accounting and Finance 6 CP EN; Advanced Accounting and Advanced Financial Statement Analysis 12 CP EN (both modules EN); AI and Computational Methods for Accounting and Finance 6 CP EN (Financial Analytics with AI EN, Blockchain/AI and Textual Methods EN); Financial Mathematics 6 CP EN; Advanced Corporate Finance (FIN I) 6 CP EN; and - decisively - ADVANCED BUSINESS LAW 6 CP taught in ITALIAN (course 25404, SSD GIUR-02/A, Prof. Paolo Giudici). So 48 of the 54 taught credit points of year one are in English, but 6 CP are compulsorily in Italian for every single student regardless of track. (b) SECOND YEAR - the language load depends entirely on the track. Professional Accounting and Auditing is the most Italian-intensive: Advanced Auditing 6 CP IT (25403), Advanced Taxation Law 6 CP IT (25406), Corporate Bankruptcy and Reorganization 6 CP IT (25414), Lab in CPA exam 3 CP IT (25431) = 21 CP of compulsory Italian, plus Italian-taught complementary options (Banking and Financial Law IT, Advanced Italian Accounting Standards IT). Finance and Financial Markets has RISK MANAGEMENT AND DERIVATIVES 6 CP taught in GERMAN (25437, Prof. Peter Alfons Schmid) as a compulsory course, plus AI and Financial Decision Making IT among the options. Business Administration and Consulting has LAB IN BUSINESS CONSULTING 3 CP taught in GERMAN (25454, Prof. Michael Nippa) as a compulsory course. Academic Writing and Research Skills 6 CP is EN in all tracks (25449, ANGL-01/C, Prof. Paolo Perego). (c) Free-choice courses published for 2026/27 are all English: Sustainability Accounting and Integrated Reporting EN, Business Intelligence and Data Visualization EN, International and EU Tax Law EN, CFA Preparation EN. SUMMARY: English is the dominant language of instruction (roughly two thirds to three quarters of the taught credits depending on track), Italian is a genuine and unavoidable second language of instruction (minimum 6 CP, up to ~27 CP in the accounting track), and German is the thinnest of the three (only 2 courses in the whole 2026/27 offering: 6 CP in the Finance track and 3 CP in the Consulting track). LANGUAGE-EXAM CHOICE RULES from the brochure: 'Students who graduated in a Ladin school in South Tyrol have to sit the English language exams and can choose between German or Italian for the others.' and 'Students who graduated in a language different from the three unibz official teaching languages must choose the two languages in which they intend to sit the language exams. They have to communicate their option to the Faculty Secretariat.' That second sentence is the one that matters for an international applicant: you must nominate TWO of the three languages, and English can only ever be one of them.
campus: Bozen-Bolzano - the main city-centre campus, Universitaetsplatz 1 / piazza Universita 1, 39100 Bozen-Bolzano, Italy. Confirmed by the brochure 'At a Glance' box ('Campus: Bozen-Bolzano') and by the Faculty of Economics and Management secretariat address. This is NOT the NOI Techpark campus (which hosts the Master in Software Engineering and Master in Computing for Data Science), NOT Brixen-Bressanone (Faculty of Education), NOT Bruneck-Brunico (Tourism, Sport and Event Management), and there is no Trento or Innsbruck component of the kind used by Energy Engineering or EMMA. Single-campus programme with no compulsory mobility. Optional mobility exists in two forms: (1) exchange programmes with selected European and international universities, and (2) the Double Degree with Baruch College (CUNY) and NYU Stern in New York, both of which are selective and taken after the first year. On-site facilities and the 24/7 emergency line for the Bozen-Bolzano city-centre campus: +39 0471 011011.
degree_class: LM-77 - Scienze economico-aziendali (Economics and Business Administration), the standard Italian second-cycle class for accounting/finance/management masters. Stated in the brochure 'At a Glance' box: 'Degree class: LM-77'. Practical consequence of the class code: under the national rule on simultaneous enrolment reproduced in the admission document, you may enrol in at most 2 programmes at the same time and the two may not belong to the same class, so you could not combine this with another LM-77 programme; the admission document illustrates the rule with the example 'LM-18/LM-18'. Note that the SSD (scientific-disciplinary sector) codes used in the entry requirements were renumbered by the 2024 Italian reform and the unibz document helpfully gives both the new and the old code for every sector (ECON-06/A ex SECS-P/07, ECON-07/A ex SECS-P/08, ECON-09/A ex SECS-P/09, ECON-09/B ex SECS-P/11, IEGE-01/A ex ING-IND/35). AlmaLaurea CODICIONE for this degree course: 0210107307800002.

Evidence: AlmaLaurea graduate-satisfaction and employability statistics are published for it (CODICIONE 0210107307800002) and the brochure cites 'the most recent AlmaLaurea survey' finding that '93% of our graduates are employed in junior management positions'; the Double Degree agreements with Baruch College (CUNY) and NYU Stern are described as established and 'exclusive'; a standing corporate sponsor list exists (bureauPlattner, Banca Popolare dell'Alto Adige, Cassa di Risparmio di Bolzano, Graber & Partner, Manteco, Raiffeisen Landesbank, Raiffeisen Verband Suedtirol, Rego, REVI & Partners, Schachermayer, Hager&Partners); and a guest-lecture programme for 2025-26 is published as a separate PDF. The exact year of first activation is not stated anywhere on the English pages [uncertain]. What IS new is the CURRICULUM, not the programme: the unibz course-offering page for this degree is split into 'Course Offering - Enrolled from 2025' and 'Course offering - Enrolled before 2025', which means a study-plan reform took effect for the 2025/26 intake and applies to the 2026/27 intake. The reformed plan is visibly modernised around AI and sustainability - AI and Computational Methods for Accounting and Finance (with modules 'Financial Analytics with AI' and 'Blockchain, AI and Textual Methods'), AI and Financial Decision Making, Sustainability Accounting and Integrated Reporting, Business Intelligence and Data Visualization, Financial Engineering and Quantitative Investment Strategies - and the SSD codes throughout were migrated to the post-2024 ECON-xx/x and GIUR-xx/x scheme. An applicant comparing older third-party descriptions of this master with the current one will find the second-year content materially different; use only the 2026/27 brochure.

The brochure: 'As well as the three study tracks offered, students have also the opportunity to create their own study plan by combining courses of interest.' Internally the course-offering page tags courses with curriculum codes 'curr. LP', 'curr. FIN' and 'curr. DCA', which correspond to the three tracks (LP = the professional-accounting/libera professione track, FIN = Finance, DCA = the consulting track) [uncertain - this expansion of the abbreviations is an inference from which courses carry which tag, not a published glossary]. english_only_accessibility: EFFECTIVELY CLOSED for a candidate whose only usable language is English. This is the single most important finding about this programme and it is backed by outcome data, not just by rules. (1) THE RULE. Entry requires C1 in a first official teaching language AND B2 in a second official teaching language, and the admission document makes it eliminatory: 'The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure.' Because the requirement is positional (1st / 2nd / 3rd language) rather than tied to named languages, a native or C1 English speaker satisfies the FIRST slot only. The second slot must be filled by Italian or German at B2. There is no waiver, no conditional language admission, and no 'you may certify it later' route: the certification is mandatory for the first and second language at application time. (2) THE 2026/27 OUTCOME DATA - decisive. In the Early Bird session, which is the ONLY session non-EU citizens living abroad may use, the non-EU section of the signed ranking list contains no admitted candidates and no waiting list at all. It contains a single table headed 'Le seguenti persone non soddisfano i requisiti linguistici richiesti per l'accesso' listing exactly two applicant IDs (153960 and 149873) - i.e. every non-EU applicant in the cycle was thrown out on language, and ZERO of the 5 non-EU places were awarded. The same filter bit inside the EU pool: 7 EU/parity applicants were excluded for language in the Early Bird session and 6 more in the Late session. (3) EVEN IF ADMITTED, THE CURRICULUM STILL BLOCKS YOU. Advanced Business Law (6 CP, GIUR-02/A) is compulsory in year one for all three tracks and is taught in Italian. Every second-year track then adds a non-English compulsory course: Professional Accounting and Auditing adds roughly 21 CP of Italian (Advanced Auditing, Advanced Taxation Law, Corporate Bankruptcy and Reorganization, Lab in CPA exam); Finance and Financial Markets adds Risk Management and Derivatives in German; Business Administration and Consulting adds Lab in Business Consulting in German. On top of that, B1 in the third language is the minimum needed even to REGISTER for the exams of courses taught in that language. (4) THE EXIT GATE. To graduate you must certify C1 / C1 / B1 across the three languages. So the second language has to be pushed from B2 to C1 during the degree, and the third from zero to B1. (5) THE ONLY REALISTIC ROUTE IN. Acquire a recognised B2 (or better) in Italian or German BEFORE the application deadline. Note two traps: the unibz Language Centre only examines at B2 and C1 (no A-level or B1 exams are offered for admission purposes), and the Additional Application Session offers no Language Centre exams at all - for that session unibz recommends LanguageCert, TOEFL or IELTS, which are English exams and therefore useless for filling the second-language slot. Realistically this is a 12-24 month preparation project, so for a candidate deciding now, treat this programme as closed and look instead at the genuinely English-only unibz masters (Software Engineering, Computing for Data Science, Data Analytics for Economics and Management, Entrepreneurship and Innovation, Smart Technologies for Sports and Health, Energy Engineering, Industrial Mechanical Engineering). COMPARISON WITHIN UNIBZ: this programme sits in the hardest language tier together with the Master in Public Policy and Innovative Governance (also C1/B2/none). It is stricter than the trilingual bachelors (B2/B2/none) and vastly stricter than the English-only masters (B2 English, no second language at all).
admission_type: RESTRICTED ACCESS (numero programmato / numero chiuso) with a merit-based ranking list produced by documentary evaluation of the applicant's study career. There is NO entrance examination of any kind: no unibz written test, no TOLC, no TOLC-E, no CENT-S, no SAT, no aptitude test, no portfolio, no motivation letter, no project proposal, no video and no interview. Selection is a points-based dossier assessment out of a nominal 100 points built from four criteria (grade average, optional GMAT/GRE, above-minimum language proficiency, and prior attendance of courses that appear in this master's own curriculum), with a hard qualifying floor of 55 points. The language requirement operates as a separate ELIMINATORY gate before scoring: failing it excludes you from the procedure entirely and you appear in a bare exclusion table with no score at all. The curricular gate (degree class L-18/L-33 or 15 CP in the listed SSDs) works the same way. TWO SEPARATE RANKING LISTS are drawn up and published in the same signed decree: one for 'CITTADINI E CITTADINE UE ED EQUIPARATI/EQUIPARATE' (EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment) and one for 'CITTADINI E CITTADINE NON-UE RESIDENTI ALL'ESTERO' (non-EU citizens resident abroad). They do not compete with each other. The selection criteria were approved by the Faculty Council of the Faculty of Economics, resolution no. 142 of 15.09.2025 ('delibera del Consiglio di Facolta della Facolta di Economia n. 142 dd. 15.09.2025'), and the tie-break procedure is governed by art. 26, paragraph 2, letter b) of the university admission regulations in force. The admission committee for 2026/27 was chaired by Prof. Paolo Perego with Prof. Nicola Dalla Via and Prof. Massimiliano Bonacchi as members; the decrees are digitally signed and appealable to the Administrative Court of Bolzano within 60 days of notification or publication.
academic_requirements: You must hold ONE of two alternative qualifications. ROUTE 1 - a bachelor degree in one of the listed Italian degree classes, or an equivalent qualification gained abroad: under D.M. 270/04, L-18 Economics and Business Administration or L-33 Economics; under the older D.M. 509/99, class 17 Economics and Business Administration or class 28 Economic Sciences; or a 'Final degree or university certificate from a School of Economics, according to the regulation in force before M.D. 509/99'. Footnote in the admission document: 'Italian citizen who have obtained their degree abroad must also have a secondary school leaving qualification.' ROUTE 2 - a bachelor degree in ANY other class (or an equivalent foreign qualification) PROVIDED you have acquired at least 15 credit points in one or more of these scientific-disciplinary sectors, quoted with both the new post-2024-reform codes and their old equivalents: ECON-06/A (ex SECS-P/07) Accounting; ECON-07/A (ex SECS-P/08) Business Administration; ECON-09/A (ex SECS-P/09) Managerial Finance; ECON-09/B (ex SECS-P/11) Economics and Management of Financial Intermediary; IEGE-01/A (ex ING-IND/35) Industrial Engineering. Note that IEGE-01/A opens the door to engineering-management graduates, which is unusual for an LM-77. TWO ANTI-GAMING RULES attached to the 15 CP: 'Courses provided by the curriculum of the Master in Accounting and Finance are not taken into account for the achievement of the 15 credits required for admission to the Master programme', and 'Courses which are recognised for the achievement of the above-mentioned 15 CP cannot be used for a possible shortening of the study career.' So you cannot use this master's own courses to qualify for it, and credits spent on qualifying cannot later be recycled into credit recognition. FOR FOREIGN DEGREES the diploma supplement must demonstrate at least 180 ECTS AND that the qualification gives access to a master programme. Documentation must be in Italian, German or English and must state: final grade, exams passed with grade and date of passing, credit points, and (for foreign titles) the grading scale of the awarding university with the minimum pass grade and the maximum achievable grade. Scientific field codes are required only for Italian titles. 'The Faculty reserves the right to request a description of the contents of the courses and/or teaching hours where necessary.' NOT-YET-GRADUATED APPLICANTS need at least 140 ECTS (see conditional_admission - note that 140 is higher than the 120 that most unibz masters require). COMPLETENESS IS ELIMINATORY: 'Only complete sets of documents will be evaluated. The absence of one or more documents required for the calculation of the grade average will result in exclusion from the ranking list.' 2026/27 EVIDENCE THAT THIS GATE BITES: the Early Bird decree contains a dedicated exclusion table for applicants who 'non sono in possesso e non stanno frequentando un corso di laurea nelle classi di laurea L-18 o L-33 e non raggiungono i 15 CFU negli ambiti disciplinari richiesti' - two applicants (IDs 144039 and 143880) were excluded on exactly this ground. LANGUAGE is a separate and equally eliminatory academic prerequisite - see language_requirements.
entry_exam_or_test: NO ENTRANCE EXAM. There is no unibz admission test, no TOLC or TOLC-E, no CENT-S, no SAT and no subject test for this programme; admission is purely by dossier evaluation. Only two kinds of test appear anywhere in the procedure, and only one of them is compulsory. (1) OPTIONAL - GMAT or GRE. Explicitly not required: 'GMAT or GRE test: maximum 20 points. It contributes to the calculation of the overall score, but is not a compulsory requirement for the admission.' Scoring: GMAT 0-490 = 0 points, 491-650 = 8 points, above 650 = 20 points; GRE 0-300 = 0 points, 301-327 = 8 points, above 327 = 20 points. Validity: 'The GMAT test will only be scored if it has been passed with a score above 490 in the 5 years preceding the selection process.' 'The GRE test will only be considered as an alternative to the GMAT test if it has been taken with a score above 300 in the 5 years preceding the selection process.' Unofficial score reports are accepted at application: 'The committee will also consider any unofficial GMAT score reports, and applicants agree to submit the official report no later than the deadline for payment of the first instalment' (i.e. 05/06/2026 for Early Bird, 06/08/2026 for Late). GMAT is booked at www.mba.com and GRE at www.ets.org/gre/. (2) COMPULSORY IN EFFECT - LANGUAGE PROFICIENCY. You must prove C1 in a first and B2 in a second official teaching language. If you do not already hold a recognised certificate or a qualifying school/university medium of instruction, the only remaining route is the unibz Language Centre proficiency exam, which is held online on fixed dates: for the Early Bird session, 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026) and 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026); for the Late Application session, 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026). Two restrictions catch people out: 'you can only register for C1 and B2 level exams' and 'only for one level per language (e.g. in the same exam session you can register for a C1 German and a B2 Italian exam, but not for a C1 and a B2 German exam)'. Registration opens only inside the windows above and only after you have created an application in the portal. There are NO Language Centre exams for the Additional Application Session - which is moot for this programme, since it is not open in that session. (3) A third test exists but only AFTER admission and it does not affect selection: a placement test in the third language for admitted students who cannot certify it, used to assign them to a learning path towards B1.
selection_scoring: NOMINAL MAXIMUM 100 POINTS, QUALIFYING THRESHOLD 55 POINTS: 'Minimum total points for admission to the ranking list: 55 points. The total score will be adjusted upwards or downwards.' (In arithmetic terms the components sum to more than 100 once the cum laude bonus is counted - 75 + 2 + 20 + 5 + 5 = 107 - which is why the document says the total is adjusted.) CRITERION A - GRADE AVERAGE, maximum 75 points. For graduates, the final degree grade; for non-graduates, the grade average of exams already taken. 'For degrees with maximum grade and distinction cum laude, an additional 2 points will be assigned.' This is by far the preponderant criterion (75 of 100) and it is also the criterion used first to break ties. CRITERION B - GMAT or GRE, maximum 20 points, optional. GMAT: 0-490 = 0, 491-650 = 8, above 650 = 20. GRE: 0-300 = 0, 301-327 = 8, above 327 = 20. Must have been taken within the 5 years preceding the selection. CRITERION C - LANGUAGE ABOVE THE ENTRY MINIMUM, maximum 5 points, using the published matrix (1st/2nd/3rd language): C1/C1/B1 = 2.5; C1/C1/B2+ or B2 = 5; C1/C1/C1 = 5; C1/B2+ or B2/B2+ or B2 = 3.5; C1/B2+ or B2/B1 = 2.5; C2/C2/C2 = 5; C2/C1/C1 = 5; C2/C1/B1 = 2.5; C2/C1/B2+ or B2 = 5; C2/B2+ or B2/B2+ or B2 = 3.5; C2/B2+ or B2/B1 = 2.5. Note that the bare entry profile (C1/B2/nothing) scores ZERO here - you only earn points by exceeding the minimum, and the cheapest 5 points come from having C1 in the second language plus B2 in the third. CRITERION D - PRIOR ATTENDANCE OF COURSES IN THIS MASTER'S CURRICULUM, maximum 5 points: 3 or more exams passed with an average mark above 26 = 5 points; 2 exams with average above 26 = 4 points; 2 or more exams with average between 24 and 26 = 3 points; 1 exam with mark above 26 = 3 points; 1 exam with mark between 24 and 26 = 2 points. In practice this favours unibz's own bachelor graduates and Italian applicants who took single subjects. TIE-BREAKS, in order: (1) higher partial score in the preponderant evaluation criterion (i.e. the grade average), as provided by art. 26 paragraph 2 letter b) of the admission regulations; (2) possession of a GMAT above 490 or GRE above 300 taken within the last 5 years - 'without the score itself conferring any further priority'; (3) the youngest candidate. ACTUAL 2026/27 CUT-OFFS (this is the practical benchmark an applicant needs): EARLY BIRD, EU and parity - 70 admitted, top score 83.15, score at the last admitted place (rank 70) 60.00, with four candidates tied at exactly 60.00 occupying ranks 67-70; waiting list ranks 71-74 scored 59.10, 58.98, 57.20 and 56.00; two applicants were excluded for falling below the 55-point floor with 54.00 and 53.86. LATE APPLICATION, EU and parity - 20 admitted, top score 80.50, score at the last admitted place (rank 20) 56.60, no waiting list. EARLY BIRD, non-EU resident abroad - no scores at all were published because both applicants were eliminated on language before scoring. READ-ACROSS: a competitive Early Bird application needed roughly 60+ points, which given the 75-point weight of the grade average means broadly a final degree grade in the region of 80% of the maximum before any GMAT/language/coursework bonuses; the Late session cleared at a noticeably lower 56.60, so applying late was, counter-intuitively, easier in 2026/27.
bonus_points: Four distinct bonuses exist and none of them is a Webometrics ranking bonus (that mechanism belongs to the Master in Software Engineering and Master in Computing for Data Science, not to this programme). (1) GMAT / GRE BONUS - the headline bonus for this master and worth up to 20 of the 100 points, one fifth of the whole score. GMAT above 650 or GRE above 327 gives the full 20 points; GMAT 491-650 or GRE 301-327 gives 8 points; anything at or below GMAT 490 / GRE 300 gives 0. The test must have been passed within the 5 years preceding the selection. Unofficial GMAT score reports are accepted for the evaluation provided the official report follows by the first-instalment payment deadline. Strategically this is the single largest lever available to an international applicant with a strong quantitative profile, and it also acts as a second-level tie-break. (2) CUM LAUDE BONUS - '+2 points' for a bachelor degree awarded with the maximum grade and the distinction 'cum laude' (in Italy 110 e lode). (3) LANGUAGE BONUS - up to 5 points for certified proficiency ABOVE the C1/B2 entry minimum, on the published matrix; the most efficient combinations are C1/C1/B2 or C1/C1/C1 (5 points), while C1/C1/B1 or C1/B2/B1 give only 2.5 and the bare entry profile gives nothing. (4) PRIOR-COURSEWORK BONUS - up to 5 points for having already passed courses that appear in this master's own curriculum: 5 points for 3 or more exams averaging above 26, 4 points for 2 exams averaging above 26, 3 points for 2 or more exams averaging 24-26 or for 1 exam above 26, 2 points for 1 exam scoring 24-26. Claimed through an optional self-declaration. Note the interaction with the entry requirement: courses in this master's curriculum cannot simultaneously be used to reach the 15 CP curricular prerequisite. NOT PRESENT: no startup/project-presentation bonus (that is Entrepreneurship and Innovation, 30 points), no portfolio scoring, no CV scoring, no interview scoring, no university-ranking bonus.
portfolio_and_materials: NONE REQUIRED. This programme demands no portfolio, no motivation letter, no letter of recommendation, no research or project proposal, no video and no CV. There are consequently no format limits of the kind that apply elsewhere at unibz (Design's 20 MB PDF portfolio, the 2-page A4 project proposal, the 6,000-character motivation letter, the 2-minute video). Selection is entirely documentary and quantitative. The only structured, template-bound upload in the whole procedure is the EXCEL FILE for applicants who have not yet graduated: 'If you have not graduated yet, you must confirm that you have acquired at least 140 credit points (ECTS) in your course of origin. Please use the excel file available in the application portal.' The template is downloadable inside the application portal only and must be filled and re-uploaded; there is no public URL for it. Three OPTIONAL uploads exist, each tied to a scoring criterion rather than to a qualitative assessment: optional language certificates (to claim criterion C points beyond the mandatory first- and second-language proof), optional GMAT and/or GRE certificates (criterion B), and an optional self-declaration listing passed exams that are included in this master's curriculum (criterion D). Two warnings are repeated twice in the admission document and are worth taking literally: 'Mendacious declarations will be criminally prosecuted and will result in the automatic exclusion from the ranking list', and on the ID document, 'if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure'. Once submitted, an application cannot be changed: 'Once the application has been sent, it cannot be modified. Filled-in forms which have not been sent correctly will not be taken into consideration.'
interview: NO INTERVIEW at any stage of the admission procedure, and therefore no published interview dates. The admission document describes a purely documentary evaluation and lists no oral stage, no conditional interview and no committee meeting with candidates; the signed ranking-list decrees likewise show only score tables and exclusion tables. This is a meaningful difference from other unibz masters an applicant may be comparing: the Master in Computing for Data Science routes below-threshold candidates to online interviews (22 and 26 May 2026), and the Master in Software Engineering uses a CV evaluation followed, if unsatisfactory, by an online interview in English for candidates below the 24/30 grade-average threshold. Accounting and Finance has no such secondary gate - if your dossier score is below 55 you are simply excluded, with the right to re-apply in the Late session (an option only EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment actually have). The only human-contact stage in the whole process is optional pre-application advice from the Advisory Service (+39 0471 012100, apply@unibz.it, or an online appointment). Separately - and after admission, not as part of it - the Double Degree with Baruch College and NYU Stern involves its own selection during the first year based on academic record and English proficiency; the format of that internal selection is not published [uncertain].
conditional_admission: YES, and the credit threshold is HIGHER than the unibz norm: 'You can apply if you have acquired at least 140 credit points (ECTS). In this case you will be admitted conditionally, and you need to submit your diploma by the enrolment deadline.' Most unibz masters use 120 ECTS; this programme, like the Master in Data Analytics for Economics and Management, requires 140. HOW IT WORKS IN PRACTICE: non-graduates are scored on the grade average of exams already taken rather than on a final degree grade, are ranked 'with reservation' ('Applicants who have not yet obtained their degree will be included in the ranking with reservation' / 'ammesso in graduatoria con riserva'), and are flagged with an asterisk in the published ranking list. The 140 ECTS must be certified using the compulsory Excel template in the application portal, and the underlying transcript of records must be uploaded as well. THE HARD DEADLINE: the degree must be obtained by the enrolment deadline of 13 October 2026, 12:00 noon. 'If you achieve your qualification after the enrolment deadline, you cannot enrol, and you will lose your place which will be offered to the subsequent applicant in the ranking list.' THE MONEY WARNING, given twice: 'Advice: If you achieve your qualification after the enrolment deadline, you should not pay the tuition fees to confirm the study place.' Because a payment made to secure a place is non-refundable, paying while knowing you will graduate late simply loses you 600 euro. THE SAFETY NET: 'You will be able to submit a late enrolment request and, only if there are study places still available, you can enrol by 11 December 2026.' Note the two conditions - the request must be approved AND places must remain. For a programme that filled its EU quota and was excluded from the Additional Session, the chance of places remaining in December is low. HOW COMMON IS IT: very. In the 2026/27 Early Bird EU list, 43 of the 70 admitted candidates (61%) carried the conditional asterisk, as did all 4 waiting-list candidates; in the Late list, 11 of the 20 admitted (55%). So conditional admission is the normal path, not an exception. A SEPARATE 'reservation' also applies to foreign-qualification holders: until the ARDI/CIMEA documentation is uploaded you can only be admitted with reservation, and 'if you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment'.
ofa_rules: NOT APPLICABLE. OFA (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi / additional learning requirements) is a bachelor-level instrument at unibz, assigned to students who fail the compulsory mathematics test in the Bachelor in Economics and Management, the Bachelor in Economics, Politics and Ethics and the Bachelor in Tourism, Sport and Event Management. The Master in Accounting and Finance admission document contains no mathematics test, no OFA mechanism and no post-enrolment remedial obligation of that kind. THE MASTER-LEVEL EQUIVALENT works the other way round and is stricter: the curricular prerequisite (a bachelor in class L-18/L-33 or at least 15 CP in the listed ECON/IEGE sectors) must be satisfied BEFORE admission and cannot be made up afterwards. Applicants who fail it are excluded outright from the procedure - two applicants were excluded on precisely this ground in the 2026/27 Early Bird session. There is no 'integrazione curriculare' pathway offered inside this admission procedure. THE ONE REMEDIAL OBLIGATION THAT DOES EXIST is linguistic, not disciplinary: an admitted student who cannot certify the third language must sit a placement test and follow an assigned Language Centre learning path towards B1, which is the minimum needed to register for exams in that language, and must reach C1/C1/B1 across the three languages to graduate. Language courses are free of charge but attendance carries a commitment (a course enrolment 'implies a commitment to regularly attend and actively participate', with 75% attendance needed to sit the end-of-course test that unlocks the next module).
language_requirements: THE DECISIVE FIELD FOR THIS PROGRAMME. Verbatim from the admission document: 'The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure: Entry level (to gain admission) 1st language: C1; 2nd language: B2; 3rd language: no level required. A B1 level in the third language is the minimum requirement for taking curricular examinations in that specific language. Exit level (to graduate) 1st language: C1; 2nd language: C1; 3rd language: B1.' THE POSITIONAL LOGIC: 'Your first language is the language in which you have the highest level of proficiency (C1). Your third language is instead the language in which you are weaker (or in which you are an absolute beginner).' The slots are assigned by your own strength, not by which language unibz prefers - but they must be filled from the set {German, Italian, English}, so English can occupy only one of the two certified slots. CERTIFICATION OBLIGATION: 'The certification is mandatory for the first and second language, for the third language it is recommended (from B1 onwards).' Certificates awarded by an Italian public institution are declared by self-declaration; those from a foreign public institution require an uploaded scanned copy of the original. Proof is submitted in the application portal under 'upload language certificates' and/or 'enrol for language exams', after creating an application under 'create/manage applications'. ELIMINATORY IN PRACTICE, not merely on paper - the 2026/27 decrees carry a dedicated exclusion table 'Le seguenti persone non soddisfano i requisiti linguistici richiesti per l'accesso e vengono pertanto escluse dal procedimento di ammissione': 7 EU/parity applicants excluded in the Early Bird session, 6 in the Late session, and BOTH non-EU applicants in the Early Bird session (the entire non-EU field). EU applicants excluded on language may re-apply in the second session and this genuinely works: applicant ID 155424 was excluded on language in the Early Bird session and then topped the Late Application ranking with 80.50 points. Non-EU applicants living abroad get no second chance because there is only one application window for them. DURING THE PROGRAMME: the third language must reach B1, otherwise you cannot register for the exams of courses taught in it - which is not hypothetical here, because Advanced Business Law (Italian) is compulsory for everyone and each track carries at least one further Italian- or German-taught compulsory course. Free Language Centre courses are provided: intensive A1 courses only in the September pre-semester window (01-18/09/2026, Monday to Friday, 6 hours a day), extensive courses of 4 hours a week during semesters, intensive courses of 8 hours a week between semesters, with the stated aim of reaching B1 in the third language after the first study year. TO GRADUATE: C1 in the first language, C1 in the second (up from B2 at entry) and B1 in the third. The second-language upgrade from B2 to C1 is a real workload item that applicants routinely overlook.
entry_levels_by_position: C1 / B2 / none - the strictest entry profile at unibz, shared only with the Master in Public Policy and Innovative Governance. 1st language C1; 2nd language B2; 3rd language no level required at entry (though B1 is needed later to sit exams in it, and B1 is the exit requirement). Certification is mandatory for positions one and two and merely recommended (from B1 upwards) for position three. The levels attach to POSITIONS, not to named languages: you nominate as your first language whichever of German, Italian or English you are strongest in. For an international applicant this almost always means English fills position one, which leaves position two to be filled by Italian or German at B2 - the actual barrier. Only C1 and B2 exams are offered by the unibz Language Centre, which mirrors the two entry positions exactly; there is no Language Centre exam at A2 or B1 for admission purposes. You may register for only one level per language per session. CONTEXT ACROSS UNIBZ so the difficulty is legible: C1/B2/none here and at Public Policy and Innovative Governance (hardest); B2/B2/none at the trilingual bachelors such as Computer Science and Economics and Management; B2/B1/none at Electronic and Information Engineering; B2/none/none at the fully English-taught masters (Software Engineering, Computing for Data Science, Data Analytics for Economics and Management). Scoring interaction: the bare C1/B2/none profile earns ZERO of the 5 available language points; you must exceed the minimum (C1/C1/B2 or better) to collect the full 5.
exit_levels: C1 / C1 / B1 - stated in the admission document as 'Exit level (to graduate) 1st language: C1; 2nd language: C1; 3rd language: B1', and confirmed by the university's trilingual-master language model: 'there are exit language requirements: in order to graduate, you will need to certify two languages at the C1 level and the third language at the B1 level.' TWO UPGRADES ARE THEREFORE COMPULSORY DURING THE DEGREE: the second language must rise from B2 at entry to C1 at exit, and the third language must rise from nothing at entry to B1. Neither is optional and neither can be deferred past graduation - these are graduation conditions, not recommendations. THE UNIVERSITY IS BLUNT ABOUT THE DIFFICULTY: 'We strongly recommend that you attend the language courses offered by the Language Centre. Our experience and data demonstrate that it is very difficult to reach the required language levels without completing your learning path. Please do not underestimate the importance of formal learning!' SEQUENCING ADVICE published by the Language Centre: 'If your third language is below the B1 level at matriculation, you should first focus on achieving B1 in this language. Once you have achieved B1 in your third language, you can concentrate on acquiring C1 skills in your second language, if you have not already certified this exit requirement.' Four targeted learning paths exist, selected according to your starting level in the third language (A0 beginner upwards), combining intensive courses in the breaks with extensive courses during semesters. All Language Centre courses are free of charge; enrolling in one commits you to regular attendance, and 75% attendance is needed to sit the end-of-course test that unlocks the next module. PRACTICAL READING: a student who arrives with English C1 and Italian B2 must leave with English C1, Italian C1 and German B1. That is a substantial two-year language project running in parallel with a quantitatively demanding accounting and finance curriculum.
third_language_exam_threshold: B1 in the third language is the minimum needed to REGISTER FOR CURRICULAR EXAMINATIONS taught in that language: 'A B1 level in the third language is the minimum requirement for taking curricular examinations in that specific language.' The trilingual-master language model repeats it: 'The Master's degree course in which you are enrolled includes a B1 level in the third language which must be achieved in order to register for the examinations of curricular courses taught in that language.' WHY THIS MATTERS MORE HERE THAN IN OTHER PROGRAMMES: the curriculum guarantees you will meet third-language courses. Advanced Business Law (6 CP, Italian) is compulsory in year one for every track. Professional Accounting and Auditing then adds about 21 CP of Italian-taught compulsory courses; Finance and Financial Markets adds Risk Management and Derivatives in German; Business Administration and Consulting adds Lab in Business Consulting in German. If Italian or German is your third language and you have not reached B1, you cannot sit those exams and your degree stalls. HOW THE UNIVERSITY MANAGES IT: admitted students who cannot certify the third language sit a placement test ('You will receive further information about the test by e-mail') and are assigned to a learning path calibrated to reach B1 as fast as possible. Absolute beginners or students below B1 are strongly steered into the three-week September intensive course (01-18/09/2026, Monday to Friday, 6 hours a day) because 'Beginner courses (A1) will be offered exclusively during the pre-semester intensive course session in September will no longer be offered during the academic year' [sentence as printed in the source]. After that, extensive courses run 4 hours a week during the semesters and intensive courses 8 hours a week between semesters. THE STATED TARGET: 'The language courses offered by the Language Centre are free of charge and aim to help the students reach the level B1 in the third language after the first study year.' In other words, the university itself plans for third-language B1 to arrive at the end of year one, exactly when the track-specific Italian- and German-taught courses begin in year two. TRAP FOR LATE ENTRANTS: applicants admitted through an Additional Application Session cannot attend the September intensive courses at all, and A1 courses then only restart in mid-October with the standard path running October 2026 to September 2027. (Academic in this case, since this programme is not open in the Additional Session.)
proof_pathways: FOUR RECOGNISED WAYS to prove language proficiency, quoted from the admission document. (1) MEDIUM OF INSTRUCTION AT SCHOOL - 'the main teaching language in your final high school year if German, Italian or English (recognised as C1)'. Ladin upper secondary schools are recognised as B2 in German and Italian. For foreign qualifications: 'If the main teaching language is not clearly stated on your high school diploma, please also upload a letter/document issued by your high school stating the medium of instruction.' This is the cheapest route to the C1 first-language slot for anyone educated in English. (2) MEDIUM OF INSTRUCTION AT UNIVERSITY - 'a bachelor or master degree in Italian, German or English (recognised as C1)'. unibz graduates must upload the certificates obtained and/or declare that they passed Language Centre exams at B2, B2+ or C1. For foreign qualifications: 'If the teaching language is not clearly stated on your University degree, please also upload a letter/document issued by your University stating the medium of instruction during your studies.' (3) A RECOGNISED LANGUAGE CERTIFICATE from the official unibz list (see certificate_rules). 'If you cannot upload the certificates, you can send them by e-mail as PDF files or deliver them in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline.' (4) UNIBZ LANGUAGE CENTRE EXAMS, registered through the application portal under 'enrol for language exams' after creating an application. 2026/27 dates and registration windows, all online: EARLY BIRD - exam 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026) and exams 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026); LATE APPLICATION - exams 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026). Two constraints: only B2 and C1 levels are examined, and only one level per language per session ('in the same exam session you can register for a C1 German and a B2 Italian exam, but not for a C1 and a B2 German exam'). If you start your application outside a registration window you must return to the portal during one of the windows to register. A FIFTH, PARTIAL ROUTE for bi- or multilingual and foreign secondary schools: 'If the foreign language proficiency levels (for German, Italian, or English) are explicitly indicated on the diploma of graduation according to the Common European Framework of Reference (i.e., B1, B2 or C1), and if all four language abilities (reading, listening, speaking, writing) have been assessed, then the indicated levels will be accepted as a proof of proficiency for the second and/or third language.' Upload the school-leaving certificate under the relevant language; the Language Centre decides on recognition. Note this route serves the SECOND and THIRD slots only, not the first. ADMINISTRATIVE DETAIL: certificates from an Italian public institution are handled by self-declaration; certificates from a foreign public institution require an uploaded scan of the original. Language Centre contact: language.centre@unibz.it, +39 0471 012400.
certificate_rules: Governed by the Resolution of the University Council no. 16/2026 ('Recognised language certificates and diplomas - Students and applicants'), published as a trilingual PDF at https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Languages/unibz-recognised-language-certificates-v2.pdf. The general dispositions are strict and several of them routinely disqualify otherwise good certificates. (1) FOUR SKILLS AND SINGLE ISSUER: a certificate must 'include the assessment in all four skills and the certificate must be issued by the certification organisation itself'. Certificates covering individual skills from different certification bodies are not accepted. (2) LOWEST SUB-SKILL DECIDES: 'If no overall result and/or level is stated on the certificate, the lowest level reached in one of the subskills is decisive for determining the level, provided that this part of the examination has been passed.' (3) NO COMPENSATION, NO AVERAGING: 'There is no compensation for failed parts of the exam and no averages are calculated unless these provided by the certification organisation.' (4) FIVE-YEAR VALIDITY, generously counted: international certificates must have been obtained no more than 5 years before submission, and the whole calendar year counts - certificates issued from 1 January of the fifth preceding year are valid for the entirety of that year. Items listed in the 'Further proofs' section of the document have unlimited validity. (5) HOME EDITION GENERALLY NOT ACCEPTED: 'Certificates issued by exam boards and obtained by taking an online exam (home edition) are not recognised, except for those explicitly indicated in the list.' Check the list itself before booking an at-home test. (6) DAAD CERTIFICATES ARE NOT RECOGNISED, and neither are course attendance certificates, end-of-course tests or exams from private education providers, placement test results, or attestations issued by individual lecturers or language teachers. WHAT IS ACCEPTED (English, illustrative): Cambridge English Language Assessment suites with grade-dependent level mapping (B2 First grade A maps to C1, C1 Advanced maps to C1, B2 First grades B and C map to B2, and so on), alongside the other major boards listed in the resolution. For candidates who need a certificate quickly, unibz itself recommends LanguageCert, TOEFL or IELTS 'as the results of these exams are generally available within a short period of time' - but note that advice appears in the context of proving ENGLISH, which for this trilingual programme fills only the first-language slot. PRACTICAL WARNING FOR THIS PROGRAMME: the binding constraint is a recognised ITALIAN or GERMAN certificate at B2 or above (for example PLIDA or CELI for Italian, TestDaF or Goethe or oesd for German - all subject to the same four-skill, five-year and no-home-edition rules). Verify your intended exam against the current PDF list before paying for it.
application_deadline_eu: THREE SESSIONS EXIST AT UNIBZ, BUT ONLY TWO ARE OPEN FOR THIS PROGRAMME. unibz publishes dates as DD/MM/YYYY; ISO equivalents given below. All cut-offs are 'by noon local time', i.e. 12:00 CET/CEST, not end of day. EARLY BIRD APPLICATION: 02/03 - 28/04/2026 = 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28 (by noon). Language exams online 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026) and 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026). Ranking lists by 27/05/2026. First instalment by 05/06/2026 noon. Enrolment 10/07 - 13/10/2026 noon. LATE APPLICATION (EU citizens only): 28/05 - 08/07/2026 = 2026-05-28 to 2026-07-08 (by noon). Language exams online 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026). Ranking lists by 30/07/2026. First instalment by 06/08/2026 noon. Enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 13/10/2026 noon. ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION (EU citizens only), 18/08 - 04/09/2026 = 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-04: NOT OFFERED FOR THIS PROGRAMME. The unibz Additional Application Session page lists 'Master in Accounting and Finance (Application NOT offered)' - one of only two programmes in the Faculty of Economics and Management shut out of that session, because the EU quota was filled. The admission-information PDF still carries the generic sentence 'The Faculty can open additional application sessions for single study programmes in August and in September if there are available places', but for 2026/27 the faculty did not open one here. MULTIPLE APPLICATIONS AND SECOND CHANCES: 'You might apply for more than one study programme. If you are excluded in the first session, you might apply again in the second one.' This is real: applicant ID 155424 was excluded on language grounds in the Early Bird session and then finished FIRST in the Late Application ranking with 80.50 points. Conversely, three applicants (IDs 153444, 154698, 151823) were excluded on language in both sessions. There is no application fee for EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment.
application_deadline_non_eu: ONE WINDOW ONLY, and it is the Early Bird: application 02/03 - 28/04/2026 = 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28, by noon local time. The admission document is categorical: 'Non-EU-Citizens (living outside of Italy). Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore.' There is no Late Application for non-EU citizens resident abroad (the Late session is labelled 'only for EU citizens'), and no Additional Application Session either generally for non-EU applicants or specifically for this programme. Missing 28 April 2026 means waiting a full year. APPLICATION FEE: 50 euro, non-refundable, described as an administration fee. Payable only by non-EU citizens living abroad. DOWNSTREAM DATES FOR THIS COHORT: ranking list by 27/05/2026; first instalment of 600 euro by 05/06/2026 noon to secure the place; then the compulsory Universitaly pre-enrolment and visa application; enrolment 10/07 - 13/10/2026 noon. THE SOBERING 2026/27 REALITY FOR THIS PROGRAMME: only 5 non-EU places existed, and none were filled. The non-EU section of the signed Early Bird decree contains no admissions table at all - only an exclusion table naming two applicant IDs (153960, 149873), both eliminated for failing the language requirement. A prospective non-EU applicant should read that as the programme being, in practice, unavailable from abroad without a certified Italian or German B2. Refund rule specific to this group: paying the first instalment is otherwise non-refundable, except 'for non-EU applicants living abroad who do not obtain the necessary documents for enrolment from the Italian authorities in their country'.
parity_of_treatment: 'Citizens given parity of treatment' (equiparati/equiparate) are handled exactly like EU citizens - they use the 80-place EU quota, may apply in both the Early Bird and Late sessions, may apply to more than one programme, pay no 50-euro application fee, and appear in the EU ranking list. Two categories qualify. CATEGORY 1 - NATIONALITY: 'Citizens from Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino and the Vatican City State.' CATEGORY 2 - RESIDENCE STATUS, and this is the one that matters for Turkish and other non-EU applicants: 'Non-EU citizens with a valid permit to stay in Italy (see article 39, paragraph 5 of decree no. 286 of 25.07.1998: permesso di soggiorno (residence permit) for work, family reasons, political or humanitarian asylum, religious reasons). In this case, you apply directly to the University as described above and must submit a copy of your valid permit to stay.' THE EXCLUSIONS ARE EXPLICIT AND UNFORGIVING: 'A permit to stay for study reasons or a visa for tourism is not valid.' So a non-EU student already in Italy on a student permit does NOT get parity treatment. If the permit has expired you must attach the renewal request. And the default is punitive: 'Please note that if you do not upload the permit in the application portal, you will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad and therefore subject to the admission procedure through the Italian authorities in your country of origin.' The ranking-list decree repeats this - a non-EU citizen who declares Italian residence but does not attach a valid permit is moved into the non-EU-abroad list. WHY THIS IS DECISIVE FOR A TURKISH APPLICANT TO THIS PROGRAMME: the difference between the two categories in 2026/27 was the difference between a real chance and none at all. A Turkish citizen holding an Italian work or family permit competed in the EU pool of 80 places across two sessions, where 90 people were ultimately admitted with cut-offs of 60.00 and 56.60. A Turkish citizen applying from Turkey competed for 5 places in a single window - and zero of those places were awarded, because both non-EU applicants were eliminated on language. The language requirement is identical in both cases; only the quota, the number of sessions, the 50-euro fee and the visa burden differ.
places_quotas: PUBLISHED QUOTAS FOR 2026/27 - three separate numbers. EU CITIZENS AND CITIZENS GIVEN PARITY OF TREATMENT: Early Bird Application 70 places, Late Application 10 places (80 EU in total). NON-EU CITIZENS LIVING ABROAD: Early Bird Application 5 places, and no quota in any later session. The brochure 'At a Glance' box summarises this as 'Places available: 80 EU + 5 non-EU', i.e. 85 nominal places. CARRY-OVER RULE, for EU and parity applicants only: 'any remaining places of the early bird application, will be offered in the late application'. WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED IN 2026/27 - and it diverges from the published quotas in a way applicants should understand. EARLY BIRD, EU/parity: exactly 70 admitted, filling the quota precisely, top score 83.15, cut-off 60.00 at rank 70 (four candidates tied on 60.00 at ranks 67-70), plus a short waiting list of 4 (ranks 71-74, scores 59.10 to 56.00) to be contacted by e-mail from 8 June 2026 if admitted candidates fail to confirm. Two further applicants missed the 55-point floor (54.00 and 53.86), seven were excluded on language, and two for lacking L-18/L-33 or the 15 CFU. LATE APPLICATION, EU/parity: 20 admitted - DOUBLE the nominal 10-place quota, which is the carry-over rule in action absorbing Early Bird places that were not confirmed. Top score 80.50, cut-off 56.60 at rank 20, no waiting list at all. Six applicants excluded on language; none excluded for score or for curricular requirements. TOTAL EU/PARITY ADMITTED ACROSS BOTH SESSIONS: 90. NON-EU LIVING ABROAD: 0 admitted out of 5 places. The non-EU section of the Early Bird decree has no ranking table whatsoever, only an exclusion table with two applicant IDs, both excluded for language. There is no non-EU section in the Late decree because that session is EU-only. THE READ-ACROSS: this is a high-volume, domestically-driven programme. It filled its EU quota so completely that unibz refused to open the Additional Application Session for it, while its small international quota went entirely unused because no non-EU applicant could clear the C1+B2 trilingual gate. Compare the Master in Software Engineering, where all 30 non-EU places filled with a 35-person waiting list behind them.
ranking_and_enrolment_dates: EARLY BIRD SESSION 2026/27: ranking list published by 27/05/2026 (= 2026-05-27); payment of the first instalment of 600 euro to secure the place by 05/06/2026 by noon (= 2026-06-05, 12:00); waiting-list candidates contacted by e-mail from 08/06/2026 (= 2026-06-08); online enrolment from 10/07/2026 to 13/10/2026 by noon (= 2026-07-10 to 2026-10-13, 12:00). LATE APPLICATION SESSION 2026/27: ranking list published by 30/07/2026 (= 2026-07-30); first instalment by 06/08/2026 by noon (= 2026-08-06, 12:00); enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 13/10/2026 by noon. LATE ENROLMENT SAFETY VALVE: candidates who obtain their degree only after the enrolment deadline may submit a late enrolment request and, if places remain and the request is approved, enrol by 11 December 2026 (= 2026-12-11). MECHANICS AND FORFEITURE RULES. Payment is made inside the application portal after selecting the study programme. 'If you do not meet this deadline, you will automatically be excluded and the next applicant in the ranking list will be admitted.' Paying does not make you a student: 'Paying university fees does not confer student status, which is only obtained by enrolling. If you pay but do not enrol, you are not entitled to a refund' - the sole exception being non-EU applicants abroad who fail to obtain the enrolment documents from the Italian authorities. Missing the enrolment deadline likewise forfeits the place to the next candidate. MULTIPLE ADMISSIONS: 'If you have been admitted to more than one study programme, you can secure your admission for a maximum of 2 programmes by paying the designated rate twice. By confirming your place, you renounce admission to the other programmes.' CONDITIONAL ADMITS: the asterisked candidates (43 of 70 in the Early Bird list, 11 of 20 in the Late list) must have obtained their degree by 13 October 2026 12:00 noon, and are advised not to pay if they know they will graduate later. TRANSFERS: students transferring from another Italian university must give the Student Office a copy of the transfer application filed at their home university at the beginning of the academic year. APPEALS: the ranking-list decrees may be challenged before the Administrative Court of Bolzano (Tribunale di Giustizia Amministrativa di Bolzano / Verwaltungsgericht Bozen) within 60 days of notification or publication.
programme_specific_dates: There are no programme-specific interview, portfolio or entrance-exam dates for this master - it has none of those stages. The programme-specific dates that do exist are the language-exam sessions, the internal governance date behind the selection criteria, and the 2026/27 academic calendar published inside the admission document. LANGUAGE EXAM DATES (online, unibz Language Centre): Early Bird - 16/03/2026, registration 02-09/03/2026; and 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026, registration 24/03-08/04/2026. Late Application - 22-26/06/2026, registration 28/05-15/06/2026. No Language Centre exams are offered for the Additional Application Session. credential_recognition: Required at ENROLMENT (not at application) for anyone holding a foreign university degree, and the route depends on the country's relationship to the Lisbon Recognition Convention. ALWAYS REQUIRED, whatever the country: (i) the bachelor degree diploma; (ii) an official translation of the degree into Italian - 'not necessary if the documents have been issued in German or English'; (iii) the Diploma Supplement, which must show BOTH that at least 180 ECTS were acquired AND that the qualification gives access to a master programme. THEN, BY COUNTRY GROUP. (a) EU countries, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein: Statement of Correspondence of the bachelor degree, downloaded from ARDI - the Automatic Recognition Database - Italy (https://ardi.cimea.it/en). (b) Non-EU countries that ARE signatories to the Lisbon Convention: Statement of Correspondence from ARDI AND a Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA (the Italian Information Centre on Academic Mobility and Equivalence, https://cimea-diplome.it/). (c) Non-EU countries that are NOT signatories to the Lisbon Convention: Statement of Comparability issued by CIMEA AND Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA. Turkey is a Lisbon Convention signatory, so a Turkish applicant falls in group (b): ARDI Statement of Correspondence plus CIMEA Statement of Verification. Both take time and the CIMEA verification in particular should be started as early as possible, well before the October enrolment deadline. RESERVATION AND RISK: 'Until you have uploaded the above documentation, you can only be admitted with reservation.' unibz runs its own checks and 'in case of doubt reserves the right to request additional documents'. If the qualification is judged unsuitable the reservation is not lifted and you are excluded - and the risk persists after enrolment: 'if you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment'. SEPARATE FROM THIS, at the APPLICATION stage a foreign applicant must already upload a diploma supplement or degree certificate (or transcript, if not yet graduated) in Italian, German or English, including the awarding university's grading scale with minimum pass and maximum achievable grades - without which the grade average cannot be calculated and the application is excluded. unibz's own recognition page: https://www.unibz.it/en/services/recognition-foreign-qualifications/ (linked from the faculty navigation as 'Recognition of Foreign Qualifications').
non_eu_visa_process: SEQUENCE: apply to unibz in the Early Bird window (only window available) and pay the 50-euro application fee; if admitted, secure the place by paying the 600-euro first instalment by 05/06/2026 noon; only then start the visa application on Universitaly. UNIVERSITALY IS MANDATORY AND SINGLE-CHOICE: 'The application on Universitaly is mandatory, otherwise you will not be allowed to enrol. On Universitaly you can apply for one study programme only.' The ranking-list decree is even blunter - failure to pre-enrol on Universitaly renders the university application and the enrolment null and void. Portal: https://www.universitaly.it/. NO GUARANTEE: 'the previous acceptance by unibz does not guarantee the issuing of the visa, which is the exclusive competence of embassies and consulates', and conversely holding a study visa confers no automatic right to complete enrolment. PROOF OF FINANCIAL MEANS: unibz states you need at least 800 euro per month for living costs (accommodation, food, study materials, leisure, clothing) in the Bozen-Bolzano area, and gives indicative totals of at least 36,000 euro for a bachelor and at least 24,000 euro for a MASTER programme - the master figure being the relevant one here - on top of the roughly 1,200 euro per year of tuition, plus health insurance and visa expenses. Student-hall accommodation is indicated in the 270-360 euro per month range. RESIDENCE PERMIT: 'within 8 working days of your arrival in Italy, you must have applied for the residence permit' - contact the Advisory Service immediately on arrival for the procedure, and hand the permesso di soggiorno in to the Student Office in person or by e-mail once issued. Renewal typically requires evidence of funds (for example an Italian bank statement showing around 7,000 euro). WORK RIGHTS: a study residence permit allows part-time work of no more than 20 hours a week and no more than 1,040 hours a year. REFUND: the first instalment is refundable only where a non-EU applicant living abroad does not obtain the documents necessary for enrolment from the Italian authorities in their country. CAVEAT SPECIFIC TO THIS PROGRAMME: in 2026/27 the entire non-EU pipeline was academic, because no non-EU applicant was admitted - both were excluded on language before reaching the visa stage. The visa process only becomes relevant once the C1+B2 trilingual gate has been cleared.

uncertainty_notes: DATA VINTAGE. Everything here is the 2026/27 admission cycle, captured on 2026-08-29 from documents whose own footer reads 'Subject to change. Latest update: 24.08.2026'. Both 2026/27 ranking lists are final and signed, so the cycle is effectively closed: the Early Bird and Late deadlines have passed and this programme is NOT open in the Additional Application Session. A candidate reading this now is planning for 2027/28, and quotas, deadlines, the language-exam calendar, the GMAT/GRE bands and the provincial grant amounts are all re-set annually. Re-verify against the 2027/28 admission-information PDF when it appears (typically from late 2026 / early 2027). WHAT IS SOLID: teaching languages, entry and exit language levels, entry requirements including the 15 CP SSD list, the 140 ECTS conditional threshold, the full scoring rubric and 55-point threshold, all quotas and deadlines, the fee structure, and every 2026/27 outcome statistic - all taken directly from the admission-information PDF, the brochure and the two signed ranking-list decrees, which for once do not contradict each other (the brochure simply reprints the admission text as pages 10-20). WHAT IS INFERRED, NOT QUOTED: (1) the expansion of the internal curriculum codes 'curr. LP', 'curr. FIN' and 'curr. DCA' to the three named study tracks - the mapping follows from which courses carry which tag, but unibz publishes no glossary; (2) the credit-weighted English/Italian/German proportions, which I computed from the per-course EN/IT/DE tags on the 2026/27 course-offering page rather than from any official statement of the language split; (3) the reading that the Late session admitting 20 against a 10-place quota reflects the published carry-over rule, which is the only mechanism that explains the number but is not stated in the decree. KNOWN GAPS. The exact year the programme was first activated is not published in English. The Faculty Council resolution 142 of 15.09.2025 and the university admission regulations (art. 26(2)(b)) are cited in the decrees but have no resolvable public URL; faculty regulations are browsable only in German and Italian through the records portal. Double Degree scholarship amounts, the number of awards and the internal selection format for Baruch/NYU Stern are not published. Provincial merit-scholarship thresholds and amounts are not on the unibz pages. Three former study-plan URLs indexed by search engines (study-plan-professional-accounting-and-auditing and its two siblings) now return 404; the live study plan is rendered dynamically inside the programme page, so the brochure is the reliable source for track structure. MINOR INTERNAL INCONSISTENCIES IN THE SOURCES: the brochure prints Internship as 5 CP in the Business Administration and Consulting track but 6 CP in the other two - almost certainly a typo, since all three tracks must total 120 ECTS. Four courses in the 2026/27 offering carry no language tag at all (Financial Engineering and Quantitative Investment Strategies, Issues in CPA profession, Lab in Financial Trading, both Modeling Financial Statement variants, Internship), so their language is unknown and my credit-weighted split treats them as unassigned. The faculty fees page dates the first instalment 13 October 2026 while newly admitted students must pay by 5 June or 6 August - both are correct but for different populations. The programme page contains the typo 'definetely'. LANGUAGE OF THE BINDING DOCUMENTS: the ranking-list decrees - the only signed legal acts in the procedure, and the only place the actual scores, cut-offs and exclusion grounds appear - exist solely in Italian and German. An English-only applicant cannot read the very documents that decide their case, which is itself a fair summary of this programme's accessibility problem.
